Order the members of an operating/arm cluster

Source: R/affiliation.R
pf_arm_order.Rd

Returns the two EINs in best-guess order. The default policy is operating entity first, switching to the arm when the grant purpose names a restricted gift — a scholarship, an endowment, a capital campaign — because those are legally the arm's job.

Usage

pf_arm_order(
  cluster,
  purpose = NULL,
  policy = c("purpose", "operating"),
  sa_status = NULL
)

Arguments

cluster

Output of pf_cluster_arms().

purpose

Character vector of grant purposes, aligned to cluster rows.

policy

"purpose" (default) or "operating" for the flat rule.

sa_status

Optional output of pf_schedule_a_status(). When given, any arm ticking Schedule A line 5 is ordered first regardless of purpose.

Value

cluster with first_ein, second_ein and order_reason added.

What is and is not established

On 15 adjudicated cases containing a co-located arm pair, the operating entity was the recipient 9 times (60%, 95% CI 32–84%) and the arm 6 times. The purpose-conditional rule scores 67%, the flat rule 60%, and the current cascade ranks the correct member first only 27% of the time. The last of those is the finding that justifies acting: the existing behaviour is anti-correlated with the answer, and either policy is a large improvement. The 60-versus-67 gap is one case wide and settles nothing — only one adjudicated case had a restricted-gift purpose. Do not read the conditional rule as validated; it is the hypothesis a larger labelling round should test.
